name: reCAPTCHA V3 for Jetpack
author: Schwarttzy

sections.description:
reCAPTCHA for Jetpack enhances your WordPress site’s security by integrating Google reCAPTCHA v3—an invisible, score-based spam filter—with Jetpack contact forms and comments (including forums). Tailored for block-based themes (e.g., Full Site Editing), it leverages behavioral scoring to block bots seamlessly. Key features:

  • Invisible Protection: Runs on contact forms and comment forms, analyzing user behavior (e.g., mouse movements, session duration) to assign a score (0.0–1.0).
  • Customizable Threshold: Adjust the score threshold (default 0.5) to fine-tune spam blocking vs. user access for both forms and comments.
  • Automatic Spam Handling: Comments with scores below the threshold are automatically moved to the spam folder.
  • Submission Stats: Tracks total submissions and logs the last 20 submissions (forms and comments) with scores.
  • Jetpack Integration: Requires Jetpack for contact form and comment protection—works with block-based forms and Jetpack forums.

Ideal for modern WordPress sites, this plugin delivers robust spam prevention for forms and comments with insightful analytics, all without disrupting your visitors’ experience.

External Services

This plugin uses Google reCAPTCHA v3, a service provided by Google to verify user interactions and prevent spam on contact forms and comments.

  • Purpose: Google reCAPTCHA v3 analyzes user behavior to assign a score (0.0–1.0) indicating the likelihood of a user being a bot. This score is used to block spam submissions on Jetpack contact forms and flag comments as spam.
  • Data Sent: When a user interacts with a form or comment field, the plugin sends a reCAPTCHA token to Google’s API (https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify). The request includes:
    • The reCAPTCHA secret key (configured in the plugin settings).
    • The reCAPTCHA response token generated by the client-side script.
    • The user’s IP address (optional, included for enhanced verification).
  • When Data is Sent: Data is sent to Google’s API every time a user submits a Jetpack contact form or a comment, and during settings validation in the admin panel to verify reCAPTCHA keys.
  • Service Provider: Google LLC.
  • Terms of Service: https://www.google.com/recaptcha/about/
  • Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Users must agree to Google’s terms of service when setting up reCAPTCHA keys. No user consent is required for reCAPTCHA v3 operation, as it runs invisibly and does not display challenges.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the recaptcha-v3-for-jetpack folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Ensure Jetpack is installed and active (required for contact form and comment protection).
  4. Go to Settings > reCAPTCHA for Jetpack in your WordPress admin to configure settings.
  5. Enter your Google reCAPTCHA v3 Site Key and Secret Key (see “How to Get reCAPTCHA Keys” in settings).
  6. Adjust the v3 Score Threshold if needed (0.1–1.0, default 0.5).
  7. Test your forms and comments—view stats and scores in the settings page.
sections.faq:
Do I need Jetpack for this plugin?

Yes, Jetpack is required for contact form and comment protection.

How does reCAPTCHA v3 work?

reCAPTCHA v3 operates invisibly, tracking user behavior to assign a score (0.0–1.0). Scores below your threshold (default 0.5) are flagged as spam and blocked (forms) or moved to spam (comments).

How do I check my site’s reCAPTCHA scores?

Submit a form or comment—view total submissions and the last 20 submissions in Settings > reCAPTCHA for Jetpack. Verify detailed scores in the Google reCAPTCHA Admin Console (https://www.google.com/recaptcha/admin).

Where do I get help?

Contact support at schwarttzy.com/contact-me/ or via the WordPress.org support forum.
